title: Power of masking methods for adaptive testing in a multivariate normal means problem
summary: Many large-scale testing procedures learn signal structure from the data to boost power. Direct data reuse can inflate Type-I error ("double dipping"), so a common remedy is masking: withholding some information during learning and using it for testing. Sample splitting masks by withholding observations for testing, while null augmentation (e.g., knockoffs or full-conformal outlier detection) masks by appending null samples or variables and withholding their identities until testing.
